title: Support multiple request directories
objective: Let `~/.llm/config.json` name request directories through the existing `requestsDirectory` string, a new `requestDirectories` string array, or both, and make `llm req <request-name>`, `llm req -h`, `llm req <request-name> -h`, `llm summarize`, and `completeRequest` search every configured directory, failing closed when a request name exists in more than one directory.

branch.name: WI-0029-multiple-request-directories
branch.rationale: Each work item is processed on its own branch.

request.text: Support multiple request directories in `~/.llm/config.json`. Keep `requestsDirectory` (string) and add `requestDirectories` (string[]). Support both by scanning both the variable and every array element for requests when resolving which `llm req <request-name>` the caller is invoking.

scope.name: request-directory-configuration
scope.description: Resolve the ordered, de-duplicated list of configured request directories from `requestsDirectory` and `requestDirectories` in the layered `config.json`, validating each entry and naming the bad key or index in CONFIGURATION_INVALID failures whose guidance mentions both keys.
scope.reason: The request keeps `requestsDirectory` and adds `requestDirectories`, and both must be honored.

scope.name: request-resolution-across-directories
scope.description: Locate `<request-name>` in every configured directory for `llm req`, `completeRequest`, and `llm summarize`; load it from the one directory that contains it, resolve its parameter schemas only within that directory, and fail with a configuration error naming every matching directory when the name exists in more than one.
scope.reason: The request asks that every configured directory be scanned when resolving which request the caller invokes; the operator decided duplicates are ambiguous.

scope.name: request-help-across-directories
scope.description: Make `llm req -h` list requests from every configured directory and report duplicate names with their directories, and make `llm req <request-name> -h` resolve the request across directories.
scope.reason: The operator decided help lists all directories and reports duplicates.

scope.name: documentation-and-contract
scope.description: Document both keys in README.md and SKILL.md, add request-naming guidance to SKILL.md, update the operator-confirmed `requestsDirectory` sections of requests/README.md, and record decision D20 in requests/decisions.md.
scope.reason: The operator confirmed the contract edit under D12, and asked mid-conversation for SKILL.md guidance that agents prefix request names with the owning repository (for example `sdlc-work-item-expand`) unless the request is truly general, such as `summarize`.

nonGoals.description: Do not edit `~/.llm/config.json` or the sdlc repository, and do not add sdlc requests.
nonGoals.reason: This work item only adds the capability; sdlc adopts it separately.

nonGoals.name: unconfirmed-contract-and-request-assets
nonGoals.description: Do not change requests/README.md outside the operator-confirmed `requestsDirectory` passages (configured root, bundle layout, trust note, processing-order steps 1 and 2, and the summarize adapter), do not change requests/decisions.md other than adding D20, and do not change the bundled request assets.
nonGoals.reason: Under D12 a contract edit needs explicit operator confirmation, which covers only the named passages.

nonGoals.name: request-execution-semantics
nonGoals.description: Do not change request-bundle loading rules, parameter construction or validation, file materialization, provider selection, or response output; do not add a library option for multiple directories.
nonGoals.reason: Only the choice of which configured directory holds a request changes.

nonGoals.name: live-provider-checks
nonGoals.description: Do not invoke a provider or add live checks; all evidence is provider-free.

items.name: request-directory-configuration
items.description: The layered `config.json` configures request directories through `requestsDirectory`, `requestDirectories`, or both, resolved into one ordered, de-duplicated list.
items.reason: The request keeps the string key and adds the array key.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A configuration with only `requestsDirectory` resolves to that one directory and behaves exactly as before, including the single-directory `llm req -h` output.

A configuration with only `requestDirectories`, or with both keys, resolves to `requestsDirectory` first and then each `requestDirectories` entry in array order; keys from different config layers combine, and a later layer's array replaces an earlier layer's array.
Entries that resolve to the same real directory (repeated paths, trailing separators, or symlink aliases) are kept once, at their first position, and are never reported as ambiguous.

A non-array or empty `requestDirectories`, a non-string or empty entry, a relative entry, an entry containing `..`, and an entry that is missing or not a directory each fail with CONFIGURATION_INVALID naming `requestDirectories` or `requestDirectories[<index>]`; the existing `requestsDirectory` messages are kept.
A configuration with neither key, or no configuration file, fails with CONFIGURATION_INVALID, and every configuration failure's guidance mentions both `requestsDirectory` and `requestDirectories`.

items.name: request-resolution-across-directories
items.description: `llm req <request-name>`, `completeRequest`, and `llm summarize` find the request in whichever configured directory contains it and never let one directory silently shadow another.
items.reason: The request asks that every configured directory be scanned; the operator decided duplicate names are ambiguous.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Requests that exist only in the second or third configured directory are loaded from that directory and complete through `llm req` argument parsing, `runRequestCommand`, `completeRequest`, and `llm summarize`.

A request name present in more than one configured directory, even where one copy is a broken bundle, fails with one CONFIGURATION_INVALID configuration error that names every matching directory, before any provider is created.

A request name absent from every configured directory fails with a configuration error that names the searched directories when more than one is configured; an unsafe name such as `../x` is rejected before any directory is probed.

`llm req <request-name>` reports a request-directory configuration failure or an ambiguous name as one configuration_error JSON entry on stderr with exit 1 instead of the generic usage error, writes nothing to stdout, and starts no provider; other parse failures keep exit 2.

A request's parameter-schema `$ref`s resolve only within the configured directory that contains it: a request in a non-first directory validates against its own `$defs` both positively and negatively, and a schema with the same `$id` in another configured directory does not affect it.

items.name: request-help-across-directories
items.description: Request help covers every configured directory and reports duplicates.
items.reason: The operator decided help lists requests from all directories and reports duplicates.

acceptanceCriteria.description: With more than one directory, `llm req -h` prints every configured directory in order and lists the available and unavailable requests from all of them, sorted by name.
A name present in more than one directory is listed only under "Duplicate requests" with every matching directory, not as available or unavailable, and the listing still exits 0.
`llm req <request-name> -h` prints help for a request in a non-first directory, and fails with a configuration_error naming every matching directory for a duplicate name, without creating a provider.

items.name: documentation-and-contract
items.description: The user documentation, the agent skill, and the operator-confirmed contract passages describe multiple request directories, and the contract change is recorded as D20.
items.reason: The operator confirmed the requests/README.md edit and asked for request-naming guidance in SKILL.md.

acceptanceCriteria.description: README.md and SKILL.md document `requestsDirectory`, `requestDirectories`, the search order, de-duplication, and the duplicate-name error.
SKILL.md tells agents to prefix request names with the owning repository name, such as `sdlc-work-item-expand`, unless the request is truly general, such as `summarize`.

requests/README.md mentions `requestDirectories` in the configured-root, bundle-layout, trust, processing-order, and summarize-adapter passages and changes nothing else; requests/decisions.md adds D20 citing the WI-0029 request and the operator confirmation; no other file under requests/ changes.
